ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: An age of great territorial powers, Egypt, the Hittites, Mitanni, Babylon and Assyria, linked by diplomacy, trade and chariot warfare.
Clay tablets of the 14th century BCE in which the pharaohs and the kings of Babylon, Mitanni and the Hittites wrote to one another in Akkadian.
Ramesses II and Muwatalli II fought one of antiquity's best-documented chariot battles in 1274 BCE, and their kingdoms later made peace.
Anatolia's great power rivalled Egypt for Syria and left the earliest peace treaty surviving in both sides' versions, until Hattusa burned around 1180 BCE.
A rich port whose last letters report enemy ships off the coast; it was sacked and burned around 1185 BCE and never rebuilt.
Seafaring raiders of the end of the Late Bronze Age; Egyptian records tell of Ramesses III defeating them on land and sea around 1177 BCE.
Drought, famine, migrations, unrest and broken trade: the debated causes of a collapse that ended the Hittite state and weakened Egypt.
Probably among the Sea Peoples, they settled the coast of Canaan in the 12th century BCE and formed a league of five cities.
Iron replaced bronze for tools and weapons from around 1200 BCE, in an age of new kingdoms, hillforts and first written records.
